small_guidance:
- Sweep BLOCK_W ∈ {16, 32, 64} together with num_warps ∈ {2, 4, 8} via `triton.autotune`; OW=33 so BLOCK_W=64 wastes lanes but may amortize the weight broadcast cost — measure both 32 and 64.
- Hoist the weight tile load out of the spatial loop: for fixed (kd,kh,kw,ic) the `w_vals[OC]` is reused across every (n,od,oh) program; consider restructuring so one program covers multiple (oh,ow) tiles to reuse weight loads in registers, or merge ic into a single vector load of shape [IC,OC]=[3,16]=48 elements.
- Try collapsing the (oh, ow) tile into a 2D output tile (BLOCK_H × BLOCK_W) per program so the inner `kh` loop reuses the same x row across BLOCK_H outputs and reduces total program count / launch overhead.
large_guidance:
- Switch from gather-style conv_transpose (current: iterate kernel taps and check stride-divisibility, lots of masked loads with ~7/8 lanes idle because STRIDE=2) to a scatter-add formulation: one program per input element computes its [OC, KD, KH, KW] contribution, but since we then need a per-(n,od,oh,ow) reduction (logsumexp over OC), instead use the gemm-style implicit-im2col where K = IC*KD*KH*KW and M = OC; with IC=3, K=81, OC=16 this is a tiny GEMM that fits entirely in registers — load weight [OC,K] once per (n, output-spatial tile) and stream input.
- Fuse better along the output-spatial axis: make one persistent program own a contiguous chunk of (od, oh, ow) for a single n, keep the [OC] accumulator vector resident, and do logsumexp + hardswish + bias + clamp in the epilogue. This removes the BLOCK_W×OC materialization and lets the [OC=16] dim live in registers.
- Precompute, on the host, a packed weight layout [OC, IC*KD*KH*KW] in channels-last-friendly order so the inner GEMM-K loop is a contiguous load; current [IC,OC,KD,KH,KW] layout makes the OC-stride large (KD*KH*KW=27) and hurts the broadcast.
